attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The SAMURAI-SEC ransomware encrypts files on local and mapped network drives, appending the .samurai extension to disrupt business operations and extort the victim.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
attack_patterns.description: Before encryption, the SAMURAI-SEC malware exfiltrates sensitive files from the victim's system to attacker-controlled infrastructure as part of its double-extortion strategy.

attack_patterns.name: File and Directory Discovery
attack_patterns.description: The SAMURAI-SEC ransomware searches the victim's filesystem to identify and locate files for encryption.

attack_patterns.name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
attack_patterns.description: Chaos-family ransomware like SAMURAI-SEC may use the registry Run key for persistence, as suggested by hunting hints pointing to 'HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run'.

malware.name: SAMURAI-SEC
malware.description: A new ransomware strain derived from the Chaos ransomware builder. It employs a double-extortion strategy by encrypting files with a .samurai extension and exfiltrating data before encryption.

malware.name: Chaos
malware.description: A ransomware builder family that allows low-skilled actors to create and deploy their own ransomware variants, such as SAMURAI-SEC.

infrastructure.name: SAMURAI-SEC Exfiltration Server
infrastructure.description: Attacker-controlled infrastructure used to receive exfiltrated data from victims before file encryption.

indicators.name: SAMURAI-SEC Ransom Note Creation
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: SAMURAI-SEC Ransom Note Creation
id: 7c8d9e0f-1a2b-4c5d-8e9f-0a1b2c3d4e5f
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of ransom notes used by SAMURAI-SEC ransomware.
references:
  - https://www.cyfirma.com/news/weekly-intelligence-report-23-oct-2026/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-24
tags:
  - attack.t1486
level: high
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\READ_ME.txt'
      - '\read_it.txt'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the creation of ransom note files named 'READ_ME.txt' or 'read_it.txt', which are associated with SAMURAI-SEC ransomware.

indicators.name: SAMURAI-SEC Encrypted File Detection (.samurai)
indicators.pattern:
title: SAMURAI-SEC Encrypted File Detection (.samurai)
id: 8d9e0f1a-2b3c-4d5e-9f0a-1b2c3d4e5f6a
status: experimental
description: Detects files encrypted by SAMURAI-SEC ransomware, identified by the '.samurai' extension.
references:
  - https://www.cyfirma.com/news/weekly-intelligence-report-23-oct-2026/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-24
tags:
  - attack.t1486
level: critical
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '.samurai'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the presence of files with the '.samurai' extension, which is a definitive indicator of SAMURAI-SEC ransomware activity.

indicators.name: Potential Chaos-Family Ransomware Persistence via Run Key
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential Chaos-Family Ransomware Persistence via Run Key
id: 9e0f1a2b-3c4d-5e6f-0a1b-2c3d4e5f6a7b
status: experimental
description: Detects potential persistence mechanism used by Chaos-family ransomware like SAMURAI-SEC, which involves adding an executable from a temporary directory to the HKCU Run key.
references:
  - https://www.cyfirma.com/news/weekly-intelligence-report-23-oct-2026/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-24
tags:
  - attack.t1547.001
level: high
logsource:
  category: registry_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    EventType: 'SetValue'
    TargetObject|contains: '\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run'
    Details|contains:
      - '%APPDATA%'
      - '%TEMP%'
      - 'C:\Users\'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects a potential persistence attempt where a program located in a temporary user directory is added to the CurrentVersion\Run registry key, a behavior common to Chaos-family ransomware.
